description.p: Aoide is a music player for the files you already have. Open tracks and playlists from the file picker, drop them on the window, or hand them over from a file manager. There is no library to import and no account to make.

Playlists are the heart of it: add, remove and reorder tracks, save them as M3U or M3U8 files of your own, and pick up where you left off next time. Aoide shows the artist and album written into each file, a twenty-bar spectrum follows what is playing, and a ten-band equaliser with presets sits beside it.
Aoide draws its own window rather than borrowing your desktop's. Several skins come with it, and more can be installed from a folder or a zip.
Create Playlist can start from picked audio files, without interrupting what is playing.
A track playing outside the current playlist is named in the footer, Next and Previous walk into the list, and a quit keeps it.
The playlist resizes from every edge and corner, and stays inside the desktop work area so its grip and the zoom controls stay reachable.
A 62.5% zoom step, for the gap between 50 and 75. Zoom no longer refuses a step just because the playlist has to shrink to fit.
Always on top works on Plasma, and the option is hidden where the desktop cannot do it. The player stays above every other Aoide panel.
The file pickers keep to the kind they asked for, so an audio file cannot be taken as a playlist.
macOS support: a notarized universal build for macOS 13 and later.
A 50% zoom step, for displays where 75% reads too large.
